newsitem.title: UK: Astronomers report discovery of two galaxies.
newsitem.headline: Astronomers report discovery of two galaxies.

text.p: British astronomers said on Thursday they had discovered two new galaxies which could provide insights into the nature of the universe.
The first was found in the little-known constellation Antlia (the "Air Pump") and thus has been named the "Antlia Galaxy". It contains about a million stars.
Most nearby galaxies, conveniently named the Local Group, are satellites of either the Earth's own Milky Way or the Andromeda Galaxy. But Antlia, about three million light-years away, is on its own.

"It is in a region of space previously thought to be devoid of nearby galaxies and is important for our understanding of the Local Group because there are very few members that are isolated in this way," the Royal Astronomical Society said in a statement.

Antlia will not have been stretched out by gravity from other, bigger galaxies so will offer interesting insights, said Mike Irwin of the Royal Greenwich Observatory who, with students Alan Whiting and George Hau of Cambridge University, reported the findings to the National Astronomy Meeting in Southampton.
The second galaxy was found just outside the Local Group and named the "Argo Galaxy". It, too, is in a region of space that is fairly empty.

Irwin said most astronomers concentrated on big, bright galaxies, but the small ones offered insights. "Despite their unassuming appearance, dwarf galaxies hold the key to many questions about the formation, structure and evolution of galaxies," he said.
They could also offer insights into the distribution of mysterious "dark matter", which astronomers cannot see but know by its measurable effects must make up the majority of matter in the universe.
